## Checks from live audits

A cached fetch and the layers above can miss these:

- Metadata outside the head: Next.js 15.2 and later [stream `generateMetadata` output into the end of `<body>`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) when it reads request data or runs uncached fetches, for any user agent missing from its HTML-limited bot list. Prerendered pages whose metadata resolves at build time keep it in the head. Googlebot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot are all missing from that list. Next.js says Googlebot reads it after rendering, but [the major AI crawlers don't run JavaScript](https://vercel.com/blog/the-rise-of-the-ai-crawler), and a parser that reads only the head loses the title, canonical, and hreflang. Fetch a URL nobody has requested since the deploy with each crawler's user agent, because a warm data cache can resolve metadata in time and pass the check while cold renders fail. [`htmlLimitedBots: /.*/`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/htmlLimitedBots) in `next.config.js` makes metadata blocking for every user agent. Every response then waits for `generateMetadata` before its first byte, so keep it to the data the page already fetches.
- Sitemap fields: Google [ignores `<priority>` and `<changefreq>`](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/build-sitemap) and uses `<lastmod>` only when it's consistently accurate, so set it from real content changes or leave it out. Pages built around images can list them as [`<image:image>` entries](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/image-sitemaps), up to 1,000 per URL. Images on a CDN host count when Search Console verifies that host too, which a Domain property does for every subdomain.
- Share previews: Next.js [merges metadata shallowly](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#merging). When setting `openGraph`, set the page's own `url` and inherit `images: (await parent).openGraph?.images` in `generateMetadata(_, parent)` to keep the hashed URL, dimensions, alt, and type. Leave `twitter` out so Next.js builds its tags from Open Graph without leaking layout titles. Add `max-image-preview:large` to the robots meta, which Google [recommends for Discover](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover).
- Open Graph image routes: a `[slug]/opengraph-image` that trusts `generateStaticParams` returns 500 for an unknown slug. `export const dynamicParams = false` in that image file returns 404 before the handler runs on Turbopack builds, though webpack drops it before Next.js 16.3.8. Don't set it on a page rendered per request, where `next start` ignores it.
- Linked images: describe the image in its `alt`. An `aria-label` on the link with `alt=""` on the image names the link but leaves image search nothing to read.
- Permanent redirects: Next.js `permanent: true` returns 308, which Google [treats like 301](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects), so don't report it as an error.
- Favicon: a robots.txt rule such as `Disallow: /favicon.ico` keeps the site's icon out of Google results, because [Googlebot-Image must be able to crawl the favicon file and Googlebot the home page](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/favicon-in-search). In our audits Search Console then listed the icon under Blocked by robots.txt. Google [supports BMP, GIF, ICO, PNG, JPEG, PPM, and TIFF favicons](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/favicon-in-search), not SVG, and reads `icon`, `shortcut icon`, `apple-touch-icon`, and `apple-touch-icon-precomposed` links, so an SVG-only icon set needs a PNG or ICO next to it, square and larger than 48x48.
- Search Console submission: submit the sitemap URL in the [Sitemaps report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7451001) of a Search Console property you own. A [Domain property](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/34592) covers every subdomain and protocol, while a URL-prefix property covers only its exact prefix. Keep the `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt as well, because Google [finds it on the next robots.txt crawl](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/build-sitemap#addsitemap) without a submission. Google [retired the sitemap ping endpoint](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/06/sitemaps-lastmod-ping), which now returns 404. Bing [retired its ping too](https://blogs.bing.com/webmaster/may-2022/Spring-cleaning-Removed-Bing-anonymous-sitemap-submission), so submit the sitemap in Bing Webmaster Tools and send changed or deleted URLs through [IndexNow](https://www.indexnow.org/documentation). The Search Console API's [`sitemaps.submit`](https://developers.google.com/webmaster-tools/v1/sitemaps/submit) automates submission. Request indexing in [URL Inspection](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/ask-google-to-recrawl) only for a few key new pages, since individual requests have a quota and repeating one doesn't speed up the crawl.
- Search Console validation: start Validate fix only for an issue a change has fixed. [Page with redirect and Alternate page with proper canonical tag](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203) are expected states with nothing to do. A validation moves from Started to Looking good once the first rechecked URL passes, and reaches Passed only after Google recrawls every affected URL. That usually takes about two weeks, but rarely crawled legacy URLs can hold it open for months. Requesting indexing for a stuck example in URL Inspection queues a recrawl. A URL that never existed, such as a literal `/*`, should keep returning 404 even though that fails its validation.
- Brave Search: there is no sitemap submission or webmaster console. [Its crawler](https://search.brave.com/help/brave-search-crawler) sends no distinct user agent and skips whatever robots.txt blocks for Googlebot, so a Googlebot block also hides the page from Brave. Submit key URLs one at a time at https://search.brave.com/submit-url, which also re-fetches a page after a `noindex` or removal.
- Stale snippets: Google rewrites the snippet from body text when the meta description only lists names, and keeps quoting old copy until it recrawls. After changing visible copy or the description, run the live test in URL Inspection and request indexing for the home page. Search Console's [Generative AI performance report](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) shows impressions in AI features, which no fetch can measure.
- Soft 404s: static hosts that fall back to `index.html` for every path answer unknown URLs, `/favicon.ico`, and `/apple-touch-icon.png` with the home page and a 200. Google [treats that as a soft 404](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/troubleshoot-crawling-errors) and wants 404 or 410, and the icon probes get HTML instead of an image.
- Host twins: check that `www` and the apex both resolve and that the one you don't use 301s to the canonical host with the path kept. A missing `www` DNS record gives visitors an error page and never shows up in Search Console.
- CDN rewrites: compare the served HTML with the build output. Cloudflare Email Obfuscation swaps addresses for `[email protected]` and a `/cdn-cgi/` decoder script, and its Web Analytics can inject a second analytics beacon at the edge.
- Share cards: Meta [rejects images under 200x200, recommends 1200x630 close to 1.91:1, and caps files at 8 MB](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/sharing/webmasters/images/), and documents only JPEG, PNG, and GIF. [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a521928) caps images at 5 MB, [Discord](https://docs.discord.com/developers/link-previews/overview) follows at most 5 redirects, [WhatsApp](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/link-previews) wants the image under 600 KB and the head within the first 300 KB, and [Apple Messages](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3156-create-rich-previews-for-messages) reads at most 1 MB of HTML and falls back to an `apple-touch-icon` of at least 108 px. No major platform renders an SVG share image. Declare `og:image:width`, `og:image:height`, and `og:image:alt`.
- Share-card composition: Open the actual `og:image` and `twitter:image` assets and inspect distinct variants at feed and phone preview sizes. Metadata checks cannot verify composition. Flag redundant printed web addresses, subtitles that repeat the headline, and text too small to read. Suggest deleting redundant copy before enlarging the main message or product visual and rebalancing the spacing. When creating or revising a card, omit redundant URLs and small subtitles by default. Keep secondary text when it adds essential context, supports standalone sharing, or is explicitly requested. Preserve the user’s branding and visual direction without requiring every card to have a headline. Report this as visual clarity advice, not a crawler requirement or a ranking fix. If you cannot inspect the image, mark this check unverified.
- llms.txt: Google Search [doesn't use it](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide), including for its AI features, so report it as optional guidance for agents, never as a ranking fix. [Spec v2](https://llmstxt.org/) orders the file as one H1 name, a `>` summary, detail paragraphs or lists without headings, then H2 sections of `- [name](url): notes` items, with skippable links under `## Optional`. A file at `/docs/llms.txt` covers only `/docs/`. Link absolute URLs, as every llms.txt example in the spec does, to `.md` copies or to pages whose text is in the server HTML. Pages can point to their `.md` copy with `rel="alternate" type="text/markdown"` and to the file with `rel="describedby"`, as `<link>` tags or a `Link` header. Keep it small enough to fit in an agent's context, and test it by asking an agent questions with only the file as a starting point.
- llms.txt checks: [Lighthouse](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse/blob/main/core/audits/agentic/llms-txt.js) runs the check by default since 13.3. It fetches `/llms.txt` from the origin root of the final page URL and, in our runs, follows redirects. It fails a 5xx, a 429, a fetch over 2 seconds, or a file under 50 characters or without a `# ` heading or `[name](url)` link, and marks any other 4xx Not Applicable. Locale middleware that adds a language prefix to every path turns `/llms.txt` into a redirect to a localized 404, which Lighthouse marks Not Applicable, so exclude the file from the middleware matcher and confirm with `curl -sI`, without `-L`, that it answers 200 `text/plain`. From this skill directory, run `node scripts/check_llms_txt.mjs <site-url>` for the spec structure, the Lighthouse content rules, and the status of the first 50 links. Then run `npx -y lighthouse@13 <url> --only-audits=llms-txt --chrome-flags=--headless=new --output=json --quiet` and read `audits["llms-txt"]`. Pin the major version: on Node below 22.19, a bare `npx lighthouse` installs 12.8, which has no llms.txt audit and returns empty `audits` with exit 0.

From this skill directory, run `node scripts/check_head.mjs <url>`, or add `--json` for the full report, to fetch a page as a browser, Googlebot Smartphone, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot, with a fresh query parameter on every request so no URL-keyed cache answers. It exits 1 on errors, such as head metadata that a crawler running no JavaScript finds only in `<body>`. It reads raw HTML, so it can't show what Googlebot renders, and URL Inspection can't settle that either, because Next.js serves Google-InspectionTool blocking metadata. Once per run it also checks, as a browser, the share images, icons, and Organization logo against the limits above, plus soft 404s, the `www` or apex twin, and Cloudflare email rewriting. Anthropic publishes no full ClaudeBot user agent, so the script uses the one seen in server logs, and a site that verifies crawler IP addresses may block the spoofed requests.
